take: Quiet Golf is the rare brand whose name is an accurate spec. Christion Lennon came from Museum of Peace & Quiet and built this with Raul and Diego Diaz around the idea that golf clothing can be considered without being loud — the owl crest, the QG monogram and the pennant are all there, and none of them shouts.
The Jagger Polo at $114 in active pique is the piece that carries it, cut for the course and fine in a restaurant afterwards.
It suits the player who wants good fabric and no branding to explain. Twenty-four pieces, from a $50 Pro Shop Tee up to cashmere, with a Costa Mesa flagship if you want to feel it first.
story_extra: Quiet Golf explained: founders Christion Lennon (Museum of Peace & Quiet) and Raul and Diego Diaz, the Costa Mesa flagship, the Old Tom Capital backing, the adidas Samba collab, and what's new in the collection. Based in Costa Mesa, California — flagship store at 2949 Randolph Ave — they built a brand around the idea that golf style should be considered, wearable, and part of a larger rhythm. The owl crest, the QG monogram, the pennant flag: every detail is intentional without being loud.

The range runs from Supima cotton polos made in Portugal to cashmere sweaters, linen trousers, corduroy jackets, and collaborations with Adidas, Seamus, and Smathers & Branson. Old Tom Capital backed them in 2024. Nordstrom, Revolve, and Shopbop carry the line. Eighteen pieces here — from the $25 incense holder to the $380 cashmere cardigan — that show what happens when golf apparel starts with taste instead of tech specs.

Updated, August 2026: since our first post the story got bigger — The Old Ghosts profiled the Costa Mesa flagship this spring, the brand closed a seed round led by Old Tom Capital while promising to protect "the pace," and the collection keeps deepening: the new Monterey Hoodie, Jagger active-pique polo, pleated shorts, and a cable-knit Montecito in bone are below, and the pennant driver cover is back in red. We've also refreshed every product link and added the brand in the wild from their Instagram.
